A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Anchored Decoding work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original risk–utility experiments, ablations, efficiency measurements, TinyComma benchmarks and supplementary analyses in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds instruction-tuned model, news-domain and downstream-task evaluations in Appendix E.3.

M1.justification: The KL-constrained fusion, prefix debt, adaptive banking, byte-level extension and TinyComma architecture remain unchanged. Appendix E.3 evaluates the existing method under additional settings.

E1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds evaluation on 560 New York Times articles from NewsSpan, TruthfulQA, CNN/DailyMail summarization and HumanEval code generation. These substantially broaden the evaluated domains and task requirements while retaining the original coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new instruction-tuned and news comparisons reuse SYSTEM, CP-FUSE and TokenSwap, while downstream evaluation compares against the existing safe and risky references.

E3.justification: V2 adds several evaluation protocols: an instruction-tuned risky-model configuration, pooled pairwise utility judging for news using GPT-4.1-mini, and downstream evaluation at k=1.5 with a stated 400 samples per task using accuracy, ROUGE and pass@1. These are additional protocols; the original experiments' settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.3 adds targeted checks of whether the tradeoff persists with an instruction-tuned model and an alternative semantic utility metric. The original objective, debt and budgeting ablations, rarity analysis and non-literal copying experiment are retained.

E5.justification: The original three-seed means, standard deviations and correlation statistics are unchanged. New Figure 13 includes error bars, but its caption and Appendix E.3 do not define their calculation or replication basis, preventing a reliable determination of whether uncertainty estimation changed.

E6.justification: V2 adds instruction-tuned and news tradeoff results in Figures 12–13 and downstream scores in Table 16. For example, Anchored Decoding versus the risky reference scores 0.139 versus 0.156 ROUGE and 0.488 versus 0.506 HumanEval pass@1. Original results, including v1 Tables 16–21 renumbered as v2 Tables 17–22, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, optimization problems, guarantees and proofs in Sections 2–3 and Appendix B remain unchanged, including the byte-level and infinity-Renyi formulations.

C1.justification: The principal claims remain inference-time copyright mitigation with a sequence-level guarantee, cross-tokenizer compatibility, TinyComma release and near-original utility while closing up to 75% of the copying gap. Abstract editing does not substantively change these claims.

C2.justification: Section 8 clarifies the conditional, nonlegal meaning of K-NAF. Appendix A.3 explicitly excludes copyrighted text supplied in-prompt and expands discussion of safe-model provenance and capability. Appendix D.4 adds an argument about shared-judge bias in relative comparisons.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 documents the LM Evaluation Harness, operating budget, sample counts and judge used for the added evaluations. Existing release information and implementation details remain unchanged. Reproducibility of the new instruction-tuned experiment is limited by conflicting Comma 1.7B and TinyComma 1.8B labels in Figure 12 and its caption.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Gao et al. (2023) evaluation-harness citation and expands Appendix A.2's distinction from expert/amateur contrastive decoding, emphasizing its different objective and lack of the proposed copyright guarantee.

P1.justification: V2 tightens the abstract, makes local prose corrections, updates the publication footer and broadens Appendix E.3's heading and organization. The main narrative and overall section structure remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 12–13 and Table 16, relocates the retained non-literal copying plot as Figure 14, and adjusts appendix table placement and pagination. Existing figure graphics and original result-table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added instruction-tuned, news and downstream evaluations provide useful evidence beyond v1's main mitigation settings, while clearer threat-model and guarantee limitations improve interpretation. The gains are limited by inconsistent safe-model labels and insufficient uncertainty documentation for the new experiments. The core method, theory and original empirical evidence remain unchanged.
